# Best portable power stations for camping

For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the best fit: light enough to carry and enough for phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP. Go bigger only if you want to run a fridge or cooler. Prices below are from the cited pages and may have changed.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 288Wh)

- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus (~$249).** PowerStationGearLab's top pick: 288Wh, 8.3 lb, LiFePO4. Its inverter is only 300W. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is mainly available through Amazon and other retailers. ([review](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus (~$269-299).** 286Wh with a 600W inverter, expandable to 572Wh. ([review](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Anker SOLIX C300 (~$199).** Cheapest of the group, with a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Buy the standard C300, not the AC-less "DC" variant. Note that OutdoorGearLab's lab testing scored it low (50/100), so it's more of a budget pick. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Bluetti Elite 30 V2 (288Wh, 600W).** TechRadar's budget pick ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)). Dealectric lists it at $289.99, or $275.50 with code **AFF5OFF**: [buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2). A kit with a 100W solar panel is $437 with the same code: [buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2-100w-solar-kit).
- **ALLPOWERS R600 (299Wh, 600W).** $219, or $197.10 with code **ALLPOWERS26**: [buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r600-299wh).

The Dealectric links are affiliate-tracked and the codes were tested in each brand's cart on Oct 25. The store's checkout has the final word on price. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/))

## Longer trips, a fridge or a cooler (1kWh and up)

- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2.** OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It has 2,200W output and fast charging, weighs 39 lb, and is under $900 on sale. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~$799).** TechRadar's camping pick, and a good van or overland size. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations), [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2.** OutdoorGearLab's best value, under $530 on sale. It has a noisy fan. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra.** WIRED's camping pick: 1,536Wh, IP65-rated, about 40 lb, ~$1,079. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))

I couldn't get direct buy links for the Jackery, EcoFlow and Anker models from these results. The review pages linked above have "check price" buttons for each.

## My pick

For most campers I'd choose the **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** or **Jackery 300 Plus**. The River 3 Plus has the stronger inverter and can be expanded. The Jackery is lighter. If you want the cheapest good option with a direct link, the **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** at $275.50 is the one.

Tip: turn off your CPAP's humidifier. It can triple the power draw, and without it a 288Wh unit should last 3-5 nights.

What will you be powering, and for how many nights? I can narrow it down from there.
